public_rationale: OpenAI says it deliberately omitted production classifiers to measure maximal cyber capability. Its later investigation confirms that other production protections were also absent. This supports Marcus's qualified description of unusually permissive testing conditions. It does not establish a mathematical upper bound or imply that OpenAI deliberately arranged the breach.
limitations: The decisive evidence is OpenAI's account of its own evaluation.
This assessment does not endorse the separate contextual assertion that no real-world incident occurred.
Whether production safeguards would have prevented this particular breach is a separate question.

our_interpretation: Read in context, this is a qualified description of a capability evaluation conducted with fewer safeguards than ordinary deployment.

Support requires evidence that the evaluation deliberately omitted relevant safeguards to reveal potential cyber capability. It does not require a deliberately arranged breach, an intention to cause harm, or a mathematical upper bound.
The target is the July 2026 incident described in the report available when Marcus posted. Later investigations may establish facts about that incident.
criteria.support_condition: The evaluation protocol or incident investigation confirms that relevant production safeguards were deliberately omitted to measure maximal or underlying cyber capability, making the reported behavior a qualified demonstration of what could happen under those conditions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The records establish that the relevant production safeguards were enabled and that the evaluation was intended to represent ordinary safeguarded deployment, undermining the factual basis of the characterization.
